prompt: What were some common ways of listening to music in rural United States in the year 1925, and how could they be hypothetically adapted so a wolf or a dog could use them to listen to music (without depending on technology invented after 1925)?
judge_reasoning: Candidate [3] best matches the prompt by listing many plausible 1925 rural listening practices (cylinders, gramophones/records, live/outdoor music, home-made instruments, music boxes, and radio) and giving straightforward wolf/dog hearing adaptations without relying on post-1925 tech. Candidate [4] is similarly strong and detailed, but it includes a notable factual error by referring to “78 rpm vinyl” in 1925 (records then were typically shellac). Candidate [1] is on-topic and reasonably adapted, but is less complete and leans on “amplified” setups that are less clearly consistent with common rural 1925 listening. Candidate [2] is the weakest: it shifts away from “common ways” in 1925 toward unconventional adaptations, and its constraints/feasibility (e.g., electricity claims) are internally inconsistent.
